chunks: And in the narration of Ismaʿil ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:
When the table is set, four angels surround it. Then if the servant says, 'In the Name of Allah,' the angels say to the Shaytan, 'Be disgraced, O wicked one, for you have no authority over them.'
Then when they finish and say, 'All praise is for Allah,' the angels say, 'They are a people upon whom Allah has bestowed blessing, so they rendered thanks to their Lord.'
But if they do not say, 'In the Name of Allah,' the angels say to the Shaytan, 'Come near, O wicked one, and eat with them.'
And when it is removed, if they do not praise Allah, the angels say, 'They are a people upon whom Allah has bestowed blessing, but they forgot their Lord.'

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ: Satan, who is repelled or invited depending on whether Allah is remembered
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: praise of Allah after finishing food
key_terms.الْمَائِدَةُ: the dining table or spread of food
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who respond to the diners' remembrance or neglect
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: invocation of Allah's Name before eating
key_terms.سُلْطَانَ: power or authority over the people eating
key_terms.شُكْرَ رَبِّهِمْ: gratitude shown to their Lord for His blessing

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about saying بِسْمِ اللَّهِ before eating and praising Allah after finishing?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of beginning food with بِسْمِ اللَّهِ and ending with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. It shows that remembering Allah at the table brings blessing and protection, while neglecting dhikr at mealtime reflects ingratitude for divine favor.
